claims.explanation: KF-38789, although annotated as a P-selectin inhibitor, transcriptionally mimics microtubule inhibitors such as paclitaxel and mebendazole, suggesting it disrupts microtubule function. Sensitivity to microtubule poisons is often linked to high expression of drug efflux pumps (e.g., ABCB1) and mutations in tubulin genes (e.g., TUBB) that alter drug binding, while protective features include mutations in apoptosis regulators (e.g., TP53) and high expression of anti-apoptotic proteins (e.g., BCL2). The selective killing pattern likely reflects these genomic determinants of microtubule inhibitor response.

features.basis: Multidrug resistance pump effluxes microtubule inhibitors, reducing intracellular drug levels.
Mutations in beta-tubulin can alter drug binding and increase sensitivity to microtubule poisons.
Loss of p53 function impairs apoptosis, reducing sensitivity to microtubule inhibitors.
High BCL2 expression inhibits apoptosis, conferring resistance to microtubule inhibitors.
MAP4 modulates microtubule stability; altered expression can affect drug sensitivity.
Stathmin promotes microtubule depolymerization; high levels may counteract microtubule stabilizers.
High TUBB3 expression is associated with resistance to microtubule-targeting agents.
MRP1 efflux pump can reduce intracellular concentrations of microtubule inhibitors.
Mutations in caspase-9 impair apoptosis, reducing sensitivity to microtubule inhibitors.
Survivin overexpression inhibits apoptosis, conferring resistance to microtubule poisons.
